title.es: Guion de una charla de dos minutos

es: Escribir el guion de una charla de dos minutos sobre un tema personal, con una apertura clara, al menos tres señalizadores, una tendencia descrita con cifras y un cierre.

teaching.en: A two-minute talk has about two hundred words, so the script must be short and clear.
teaching.es: Una charla de dos minutos tiene unas doscientas palabras, así que el guion debe ser corto y claro.
teaching.explanationEs: Script: el texto que escribes para decir en voz alta; frases cortas, una idea por frase.
segments: A two-minute talk has about two hundred words,
so the script must be short and clear.
teaching.audioText: A two-minute talk has about two hundred words, so the script must be short and clear.

teaching.en: She begins by greeting the audience and naming her topic.
teaching.es: Ella empieza saludando al público y nombrando su tema.
teaching.explanationEs: Apertura: saludo + tema; el público debe saber de qué vas a hablar.
teaching.audioText: She begins by greeting the audience and naming her topic.

teaching.en: She will introduce each point with a phrase such as firstly or now let's move on.
teaching.es: Presentará cada punto con una frase como «firstly» o «now let's move on».
teaching.explanationEs: Introduce each point: los señalizadores de la clase 86 sirven para esto.
segments: She will introduce each point with a phrase
such as firstly or now let's move on.
teaching.audioText: She will introduce each point with a phrase such as firstly or now let's move on.

teaching.en: Her script describes a trend: the number of members rose from twelve to thirty in a year.
teaching.es: Su guion describe una tendencia: el número de socios subió de doce a treinta en un año.
teaching.explanationEs: La tendencia lleva un verbo de cambio, from… to… y un periodo.
segments: Her script describes a trend: the number of members
rose from twelve to thirty in a year.
teaching.audioText: Her script describes a trend: the number of members rose from twelve to thirty in a year.

teaching.en: A good speaker keeps a steady pace and makes a short pause after each key point.
teaching.es: Un buen orador mantiene un ritmo constante y hace una breve pausa después de cada punto clave.
teaching.explanationEs: Pace: velocidad al hablar; pause: parada breve que deja pensar al público.
segments: A good speaker keeps a steady pace and
makes a short pause after each key point.
teaching.audioText: A good speaker keeps a steady pace and makes a short pause after each key point.

teaching.en: I always rehearse aloud so that my script fits into two minutes.
teaching.es: Siempre ensayo en voz alta para que mi guion quepa en dos minutos.
teaching.explanationEs: Rehearse aloud: ensayar diciendo el texto en voz alta para medir el tiempo.
segments: I always rehearse aloud so that
my script fits into two minutes.

prompt.es: Elige la apertura más adecuada para una charla de dos minutos.

feedback.es: Una buena apertura saluda, nombra el tema y anuncia cuántos puntos habrá. To sum up es una fórmula de cierre y Hello. Football. Thank you. no presenta nada.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que describe esta tendencia en el guion.

choices.text: Our club more than doubled, rising from 12 to 30 members.
Our club fell sharply from 30 to 12 members.
Our club stayed steady at 12 members.

feedback.es: Rising from 12 to 30 describe una subida con punto de partida y de llegada; more than doubled es la aproximación exacta. Las otras frases invierten o niegan los datos.

prompt.es: Elige el guion con mejor estructura de apertura, desarrollo y cierre.

choices.text: Swimming is fun. Thank you. Firstly, the club has twelve members.
Good afternoon, everyone. My topic is swimming. Firstly, the club is growing: it rose from twelve to thirty members. To sum up, swimming is popular. Thank you.
To sum up, the club grew. Good afternoon, everyone. My topic is swimming.

feedback.es: El primer guion saluda, anuncia el tema, avanza con un señalizador y una cifra, y cierra con To sum up. Los otros dos desordenan las partes o no tienen apertura.

prompt.es: Completa: «El público sigue mejor una charla con un ritmo tranquilo.»

feedback.es: La audience es el público; un ritmo tranquilo (calm pace) le permite seguir la charla con más facilidad.

origin.text: The ___ follows the talk better at a calm pace.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Ahora pasemos a la segunda parte de mi charla.»

answer.text: Now let's move on to the second part of my talk

feedback.es: Now let's move on to + parte es el señalizador de transición; of my talk cierra la frase.

prompt.es: Escribe el guion de tu charla con tres señalizadores y una tendencia.

answer.text: Good morning, everyone. My topic today is our school book club, and I will cover three points: how it started, how it has grown and what we plan to do next. Firstly, let me explain how it started. Two years ago, only twelve students came to the first meeting, and we sat in the corridor because we had no room. Now let's move on to the second point: how the club grew. As you can see in my chart, the number of members rose steadily, from twelve to thirty in two years. Roughly half of them are first-year students, and nearly a third are boys. This suggests that the club is becoming more popular, and it may grow even more next year. Finally, let me tell you about our plan. We would like to organise a reading night in June and invite two other schools. To sum up, the club started small, grew steadily and is ready for a new challenge. Thank you for listening. I am happy to answer any questions.
accepted: Good morning, everyone. My topic today is our school book club, and I will cover three points: how it started, how it has grown and what we plan to do next. Firstly, let me explain how it started. Two years ago, only twelve students came to the first meeting, and we sat in the corridor because we had no room. Now let's move on to the second point: how the club grew. As you can see in my chart, the number of members rose steadily, from twelve to thirty in two years. Roughly half of them are first-year students, and nearly a third are boys. This suggests that the club is becoming more popular, and it may grow even more next year. Finally, let me tell you about our plan. We would like to organise a reading night in June and invite two other schools. To sum up, the club started small, grew steadily and is ready for a new challenge. Thank you for listening. I am happy to answer any questions.

Hello, everyone, and welcome. Today I want to present my hobby, which is running, and I will outline the talk in three parts: why I started, how my training changed and my next goal. Firstly, I started running two years ago because I wanted to feel healthier. At the beginning, I could run for only ten minutes without stopping. Let's move on to the second part: my training. As you can see in my chart, my weekly distance rose gradually, from roughly five to around twenty kilometres in one year. I also make a short pause between exercises, and I keep a steady pace. Now I'd like to turn to my goal for next year. I am likely to run a half marathon in the spring, and my friends will run with me. To sum up, running is cheap, simple and good for the head as well as for the body. Thank you very much for listening. Are there any questions?

feedback.es: Un buen guion abre con saludo y tema, usa al menos tres señalizadores, describe una tendencia con cifras y cierra con To sum up y una invitación a preguntas.

origin.text: Elige un tema personal (un hobby, un club, tu ciudad) y escribe el guion de una charla de dos minutos, de 150 a 220 palabras. Incluye: una apertura con saludo y tema, al menos tres señalizadores (firstly, now let's move on to, to sum up…), una tendencia con cifras (rose from… to…) y un cierre claro con una invitación a preguntas.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que describe una tendencia con aproximación.

choices.text: Attendance was very good and everyone was happy.
Attendance is an important word in my talk.
Attendance rose gradually, from roughly 40 to around 60 people.

feedback.es: Rose gradually, from roughly 40 to around 60 combina verbo de cambio, adverbio y aproximaciones; las otras dos frases no describen ninguna cifra.
Después de la preposición for, el verbo va en -ing: Thank you for listening. Es la despedida habitual de una charla.
